2607.08003.title: Reaction-network reasoning with frontier models for experimentally confirmed catalyst-selectivity hypotheses
2607.08003.paper_summary: Catalysts are essential for sustainable chemical manufacturing, yet discovering novel architectures remains a bottleneck dominated by trial-and-error experimentation and computationally intensive screening. In complex reactions such as electrochemical carbon dioxide reduction, product selectivity is governed by dynamic interfacial, electrolyte, and potential factors as well as kinetic pathway competition. Conventional descriptor-based machine learning and computational potentials struggle to resolve these mechanistic branch points, primarily relying on static ground-state descriptors or bulk structural correlations rather than end-to-end topological pathway analysis. Here, we show that frontier language models, when strictly constrained to reason over explicit reaction networks, can discover novel catalysts by identifying the physical levers that govern pathway competition. We developed a human-AI co-thinking framework that enforces network invariance to extract testable hypotheses from complex chemical graphs. Applied to CO2 electroreduction, the framework identified ketene desorption and hydroxide capture as the acetate-forming pathway, and predicted a distinct adsorbed CO and CH2 coupling route to ketene. By isolating actionable control levers, specifically local alkalinity, controlled iron incorporation, and restricted interfacial proton-donor accessibility, the framework guided the prospective synthesis of a copper-iron oxide catalyst demonstrating a threefold increase in acetate selectivity over matched Cu-rich baselines. This mechanism-guided reasoning architecture shifts the computational paradigm from retrospective statistical prediction to forward-looking hypothesis generation, providing a broadly applicable blueprint for mechanism-guided materials discovery.
2607.08003.paper_summary_zh: 催化劑對於可持續化學製造至關重要，但發現新穎的結構仍然是一個瓶頸，這一過程主要依賴於試錯實驗和計算密集型篩選。在複雜反應中，如電化學二氧化碳還原，產物選擇性受動態界面、電解質和潛在因素以及動力學途徑競爭的影響。傳統的基於描述符的機器學習和計算潛能難以解析這些機制分支點，主要依賴靜態基態描述符或體積結構相關性，而不是端到端的拓撲途徑分析。在這裡，我們展示了前沿語言模型在嚴格限制於明確反應網絡進行推理時，可以通過識別控制途徑競爭的物理杠杆來發現新穎的催化劑。我們開發了一個人類-AI共同思考框架，強制執行網絡不變性，以從複雜的化學圖中提取可測試的假設。應用於CO2電還原，該框架識別了酮烯脫附和氫氧化物捕獲作為生成醋酸的途徑，並預測了一條將吸附的CO和CH2耦合到酮烯的不同路徑。通過孤立可操作的控制杠杆，具體包括局部鹼度、控制鐵的掺入和限制界面質子供體的可及性，該框架指導了銅鐵氧化物催化劑的前瞻性合成，顯示出相較於匹配的銅富基準，醋酸選擇性提高了三倍。這種機制引導的推理架構將計算範式從回顧性統計預測轉變為前瞻性假設生成，為機制引導的材料發現提供了一個廣泛適用的藍圖。
